notes.summary: Proved exact continuous-PC criterion: convexity on complete branches plus a common ambient supporting form at every crossing, with arbitrary branch dependencies and legal rational violations.
notes.detailedSummary: Inherited feasible rational midpoint triples imply full branch convexity without coarsening. Finite convex subgradients are nonempty compact and represent continuous directional derivatives. A compact product versus closed restriction-subspace alternative gives a zero-sum negative-cost tuple if no common support exists. Rational kernel approximation and a common small rational scale yield an actual finite printed violation. Branch Jensen and crossing supports prove sufficiency on every rational carrier.
notes.text:
Let X be the finite union of distinct complete rational affine d-planes, d>=1, with pairwise intersections empty or single points. Rational elimination makes all meeting points rational. Let V be that finite set and I(v) the incident branches. The following criterion is proved: f in C(X) is printed-PC exactly when each restriction f_i is ordinary convex and each v has one ambient real linear form p_v with f_i(x)>=f(v)+p_v(x-v) for all i in I(v), x in Q_i. Branch values agree by single-valuedness. Different vertices can use different forms.

First, rational points are dense in the minimal face of every rational feasible polyhedron: impose the active inequalities as rational equalities, solve their affine system in a rational basis, and approximate the actual coordinates; inactive strict slacks persist. Rational homogeneous cones are finitely generated by removing rational lineality, taking a bounded section with a positive rational form and decomposing that section into its finitely many full-rank active-constraint vertices. The decomposition follows by moving in both directions in a nonvertex active kernel until new constraints become active. Add both lineality signs. A finitely generated cone, also with real generators, is closed: eliminate dependent active columns in nonnegative representations until only independent columns remain. Their inverse maps bound coefficients by the represented norm. Only finitely many subsets occur, so a convergent sequence has a convergent coefficient subsequence. Homogenization gives vertex hull plus recession; finite elimination of auxiliary nonnegative coefficients gives a finite half-space description of hull-plus-cone sets.

Fix an inherited rational carrier and x in a branch, with minimal center face tau. A small ball misses every closed cell not containing x; all remaining cells contain tau. For short branch w choose incident endpoint cells sigma+ and sigma- containing x+w and x-w. The feasible triples are the rational polyhedron {(z,u):z in tau, z+u in sigma+, z-u in sigma-}. Approximate (x,w) inside it by rational (z,u). Their exact rational endpoints z+u,z-u with weights1/2 give a legal inherited PCC centered at z. Continuity gives the local midpoint inequality at x, including irrational centers and meeting vertices. No coarsening occurs.

This pointwise local inequality implies convexity on any full branch segment. Subtract its chord to get continuous q with zero endpoints. If q is positive inside, choose epsilon>0 small enough that q(t)+epsilon t^2 exceeds both endpoint values somewhere. At an interior maximum its local midpoint average at t±s must be at least its maximum plus epsilon s^2, contradicting maximality. Thus every branch chord bounds f above. This avoids an unproved uniform-local-radius assertion.

The needed ordinary convex facts also have finite proofs. A finite convex function on a complete space is locally Lipschitz: a cube's vertex values bound it above, reflection gives a lower bound on a smaller cube, and extension by a fixed radius bounds secants between close points by oscillation/radius times distance. Its derivative h(w)=lim_(t downarrow0)(f(a+tw)-f(a))/t exists by secant monotonicity, is finite by Lipschitzness, homogeneous by rescaling, and subadditive by the inequality f(a+t(v+w))<=half f(a+2tv)+half f(a+2tw). Its norm bound gives continuity.

A finite continuous convex function has a touching affine support at every graph point. Project (x,F(x)-1/n) to its closed epigraph. A nearest point exists on a bounded closed ball; squared-distance first variation supplies a unit separating normal. A convergent subsequence of those normals gives a nonzero support normal at (x,F(x)). Its height coefficient is negative: upward closure makes it nonpositive, and a zero height coefficient would give a nonzero horizontal bound on the entire spatial domain. Divide to get an affine minorant. Apply this to sublinear h at w. Homogeneity forces zero intercept, giving an ell<=h with ell(w)=h(w). The forms ell<=h are exactly the branch subdifferential K at a, since h(x)<=f(a+x)-f(a). Both signs of the Lipschitz bound make K bounded; inequalities make it closed convex. Thus K is nonempty compact and h(w)=max_(ell in K)ell(w).

Translate a meeting v to zero and set a=f(v). Put K=product K_i in W=product L_i*, where L_i is its incident tangent space, and S=image(E*->W) of ambient restriction. S is a closed linear subspace by finite-dimensional elimination. If K misses S, minimize squared orthogonal-projection norm on compact K. At its minimizer k0, q=projection_(Sperp) k0 is nonzero and first variation gives <q,k>>=||q||^2 for every k in K. Hence z=-q annihilates S and max_K<z,k><0. Identifying W* with tuples w_i in L_i gives the actual AMBIENT equation sum_i w_i=0 and sum_i h_i(w_i)<0. No grouping of branch means as a direct sum is used.

The branch matrices are rational, so this exact ambient-sum kernel has a rational basis. Approximate the tuple within the kernel by rational tuples, preserving strict negative cost by continuity. Discard zero entries. For one sufficiently small positive rational t, every endpoint v+tw_i lies in a cell incident to v, and sum_i(f_i(v+tw_i)-a)=t sum_i h_i(w_i)+o(t)<0. Finite nonincident branches/cells have positive distance, so all endpoints use the actual star. Equal weights1/m have exact rational barycenter v and violate the printed inequality. Thus K intersects S, and an ambient preimage supplies p_v globally on each complete convex incident branch.

For sufficiency, every positive-dimensional convex cell is contained in one branch. Its relative interior cannot be covered by finitely many proper affine subspaces: the product of their nonzero defining equations is not identically zero on its affine hull. Cells from distinct branches can share only a meeting point, so such a point is a vertex in every complex. A PCC centered outside V has all incident endpoint cells in its unique branch and uses ordinary Jensen. At v every endpoint is in an incident branch; sum the common-support inequalities and cancel p_v by the ambient barycenter. This works on every rational carrier, even for real endpoints. No ambient convex extension of f on the entire union is claimed.

notes.summary: Proved full-affine global approximation from ABOVE with every prescribed finite rational sample touched exactly, actual irrational recession allowed and genuine rational spatial lower faces.
notes.detailedSummary: The actual reference polytope is never rounded. Whole-boundary conjugate continuity and compactness select finite rational spatial samples with real heights. A closed sample hull plus exact recession epigraph has the required global conjugate error. Its exposed lower faces project to rational hulls/cones and preserve incidences. Appending contacts keeps global error, exact recession and every support minorant; no positive-dimensional overlap interpolation follows.
notes.text:
Work on a complete saturated rational affine branch in rational translated coordinates R^d. Let gamma be the actual finite continuous convex REAL PA positive-growth reference on a rational carrier, and let f be convex with |f-gamma|<=C. The convex/support facts of n2 apply.

The affine expression on each full-dimensional gamma cell is a global support: propagate its local equality along secants to any other point. Taking all finitely many such expressions gives gamma(x)=max_j(a_j.x+b_j), with ACTUAL real gradients. Let h(x)=max_j a_j.x and Delta=conv{a_j}. Then |gamma-h|<=max|b_j| and |f-h|<=D globally. Finitely many cell recession cones cover R^d: for any v a sequence t_n v going to infinity has a subsequence in one cell, and dividing its rational affine constraints by t_n gives v in that cell's recession cone. On it h equals that cell gradient. Positive growth gives h(v)>0 for v!=0, hence h>=b||v|| for b>0 by compactness of the unit sphere; support separation shows Delta contains a ball around zero.

Each carrier cell is pointed: a lineality direction and its negative would have opposite linear slopes, contradicting positivity of both. Its recession cone has finite rational generators by n2. On each cone h is linear, so conic decomposition of a spatial vector lifts with exact height. Consequently E_h=epi h is generated EXACTLY by finitely many (r,h(r)), r rational, and (0,1). Heights may be irrational. No rational-polyhedron claim in R^(d+1) is made, and the actual gradient polytope is not replaced.

Define f*(p)=sup_x(p.x-f(x)). For p in Delta, p.x<=h(x), giving -f(0)<=f*(p)<=D. Outside Delta a separating direction v has p.v>h(v), so testing tv makes f* infinite. The supremum is convex and lower semicontinuous. It is continuous on the WHOLE closed Delta, not only its interior. Indeed any finite lsc convex g on a compact polytope is bounded above by its largest vertex value M. At p choose r>0 smaller than every inactive inequality slack divided by its covector norm, in the polytope's affine span. If q is nearby feasible, z=p+r(q-p)/||q-p|| remains feasible: active inequalities hold along its direction, inactive ones by the chosen slack. Writing q=(1-t)p+tz with t=||q-p||/r gives g(q)<=g(p)+t(M-g(p)). This proves the upper limit inequality; lsc proves the lower one. Degenerate affine spans and singleton polytopes are handled in their own spaces.

The supremum defining f* can use rational spatial x by continuity of f. For each p choose rational x with p.x-f(x)>f*(p)-eta/2. Whole-Delta continuity preserves error <eta on a relative neighborhood of p. Compactness gives finitely many samples A0. Append every prescribed point of a finite B subset Q^d and one rational point if needed to make A nonempty. Every extra term remains <=f*. Thus on ALL Delta,
 f*(p)-eta <= g_A(p):=max_(x in A)(p.x-f(x)) <= f*(p).
All sample heights are the actual real f(x).

Let E_A=conv{(x,f(x)):x in A}+E_h. The compact first summand plus closed finitely generated cone is closed: use a convergent subsequence of bounded first summands. It is a finite real polyhedron by the finite auxiliary-variable elimination in n2. It projects onto all R^d and is upward closed. It lies inside epi f. To prove this, convex secants give f(y+v)<=f(y)+h(v): its increment at t=1 is no larger than its recession limit h(v), which follows from |f-h| bounded and the finite maximum formula for h(y+tv). Convex combinations of sample lifts lie above f at their spatial combination; adding (v,s) in epi h keeps them above f by that inequality.

Every fiber of E_A therefore has a finite attained lower height; write E_A=epi F_A. It is finite convex and hence continuous by n2. Inclusion gives F_A>=f, and the inclusion of every (b,f(b)) forces F_A(b)=f(b) exactly for all b in B. Its conjugate is g_A on Delta and infinite outside: the support functional (p,-1) on the sample hull gives g_A, while on E_h it has supremum zero precisely when p.v<=h(v) for every v, and infinity otherwise.

The touching-support argument of n2 proves elementary biconjugacy for any finite continuous convex H: the conjugate definition gives H>=sup_p(p.x-H*(p)); a touching affine minorant yields equality. Apply it to f and F_A, with their identical conjugate domain Delta. The uniform dual error gives f<=F_A<=f+eta on ALL R^d. This is a global bound with unchanged recession, not compact convergence.

The spatial carrier is genuinely rational. An exposed lower face of E_A, exposed by (p,-1), is the selected sample-hull face plus the zero-functional face of E_h. It is generated by subsets of sample lifts and recession lifts; (0,1) is excluded. Its spatial projection is therefore a convex hull of rational sample positions plus a cone of rational spatial rays. It is a rational polyhedron despite real heights. On this face the graph height is one affine function, so projection is an affine isomorphism. Finitely many lower faces cover the graph because each graph point has a touching nonvertical support. The intersection of projected faces is the projection of their graph intersection, since height over a point is unique; the affine face isomorphisms preserve common-face incidences. Including all their faces gives a finite rational spatial complex covering R^d on which F_A is REAL PA. This avoids declaring the irrational walls of an arbitrary maximum primitive.

Finally rec(E_A)=E_h: one inclusion is immediate; for the other divide a ray of translates by its parameter, use boundedness of the sample hull and closedness of the cone. Also the global bounded error directly gives F_A^infinity=h. Convexity gives printed-PC, and the same bound gives bounded difference from the SAME actual gamma. Since F_A>=f, every affine support minorant of f is retained. Appending B changed none of the error, recession or supports. This proves simultaneous finite exact contacts, not exact agreement on any infinite overlap.

notes.text:
Let X be the finite union of distinct COMPLETE rational affine d-planes, d>=1, whose pairwise intersections are empty or single points. Use the actual sum [X]=sum_i c_i[Q_i], c_i>0 REAL. It is effective balanced: on any refined complete plane each facet has equal weights and opposite primitive quotient normals; for d=1 at a crossing each complete line's two directions cancel separately. For d>1 isolated crossings are not top facets. Subtracting a branch summand leaves an effective balanced residual. This verifies the geometric hypotheses without assuming independence.

Take any actual continuous REAL finite PA PC positive-growth gamma on rational geometry and any f in C(X) intersect printed-PC with ||f-gamma||<=C. By n2 the branch restrictions are ordinary convex and each crossing v has a common ambient support p_v. Apply n3 separately on every complete branch with eta_n=2^(-n), appending ALL points of V intersect Q_i to its rational sample set. This yields actual finite convex REAL PA F_i,n with f_i<=F_i,n<=f_i+eta_n and F_i,n(v)=f(v). Every common support f(v)+p_v(x-v) remains a minorant because the approximation is from ABOVE.

Refine each branch carrier by the d rational coordinate hyperplanes x_j=v_j through every incident rational crossing. Their intersection makes v a vertex. If necessary also intersect with the inherited carrier, using only refinements. The union is a finite rational complex: distinct-branch cells can meet only at such a vertex, which is a common face. Within a branch all incidences were already valid. Equal exact crossing values glue the F_i,n continuously to a single finite REAL PA F_n, and retained supports plus the criterion of n2 prove PC at every center on every rational carrier. Finitely many branches give the one global error 0<=F_n-f<=eta_n. Each recession is exactly that of the ACTUAL gamma branch.

Set G_n=F_n+4eta_n. Values and support intercepts at every crossing shift by the same constant, so G_n stays actual REAL PA PC on rational geometry. Globally,
 4eta_n <= G_n-f <= 5eta_n,
 G_(n+1)-f <= (5/2)eta_n < 4eta_n <= G_n-f.
Thus G_n is strictly decreasing everywhere to f, uniformly on the entire unbounded X. For n>=1 the common reference bound is C+5/2. The recession is unchanged. Conversely uniform limits in this relative domain are continuous and pass every fixed finite printed inequality to the limit. Hence D_R(gamma) equals exactly the continuous printed-PC functions at bounded distance from that same gamma.

For EVERY u in C_b(X), the exact R230 grant of n1 now applies: finite rational positive balanced embedded geometry, continuous actual PC reference and bounded continuous obstacle have been verified. It identifies the actual unrestricted envelope f=P_gamma(u), including discontinuous original competitors, as continuous PC with ||f-gamma||<=||u||. Apply the preceding construction to THIS actual function. There is no global C_b obstacle-density assumption, PA-obstacle restriction, separable ansatz, coefficient rounding or local-only completion.

Only after the explicit global decreasing sequence exists do we apply S272 of n1. Every such endpoint, and every tuple of continuous relative PC functions, is in the genuine raw mixed domain, with positive finite Radon measure of mass deg_raw(gamma). Its fixed-C height and weak/BL restrictions remain unchanged. For uniformly convergent C_b obstacles, R230 gives uniformly convergent envelopes with one bound; their bounded continuous gaps converge uniformly, and S272 weak C_b convergence with common mass passes contact integrals. This proves convergence of integrals, not their vanishing.

The theorem includes one branch, disjoint arrangements, dependent branches and several distinct meetings. It excludes positive-dimensional overlaps and abstract compact categories. Candidate=false even with this scoped theorem proved. Original P05.1 and P05.2 remain OPEN.

notes.summary: Exact dependent R4 negative PCC and crossing negative-contact witnesses for every actual REAL reference, with saturated raw determinant factors, repeated zero and d! surviving orders.
notes.detailedSummary: Shared values alone fail: the explicit rational PCC has average −1/6 and no common ambient support. Every crossing supplies a rational transverse-line flat germ and positive complete-plane raw subcycle with effective balanced residual. notes.text:
The exact dependent example is in rational R4 with Q1={(x,y,0,0)}, Q2={(0,0,z,w)}, Q3={(t,s,t,s)}, weight1 on each complete plane. Pairwise intersections are zero but their sum is dependent. The actual reference gamma1=|x|+|y|, gamma2=|z|+|w|, gamma3=|t|+|s| is rational-geometry PA with positive growth and common support0, hence PC by n2. Define f1=|x-1|+|y|-1, f2=|z-1|+|w|-1, f3=|t|+|s|. It is continuous finite rational PA, convex on each branch, agrees at0 and has -2<=f-gamma<=0. At a=(1/2,0,0,0), b=(0,0,1/2,0), c=(-1/2,0,-1/2,0), values are -1/2,-1/2,1/2. Their equal-weight barycenter is exactly0 and average -1/6<f(0). The rational quadrant/shifted-wall cells containing them are incident to0, so the violation is legal. An ambient support would have x and z coefficients -1; its Q3 t coefficient would be -2, outside the subgradient interval[-1,1]. Thus shared values alone do not suffice. This is a non-PC diagnostic, not a counterexample to n4.

Replacing Q3 by {(t,s,t+1,s)} gives the distinct pairwise meeting points0,(-1,0,0,0),(0,0,1,0). This checks that n4 genuinely handles several vertices and cannot be reduced to one common origin.

The raw operator is the saturated primitive inward formula
 D_f c(tau)=sum_(sigma>tau)c(sigma) f_sigma(n_sigma/tau) - f_tau(sum_(sigma>tau)c(sigma)n_sigma/tau),
using linear parts and N_sigma=N intersect span(sigma-sigma). Tangent changes of lifts cancel because affine restrictions agree. No extra factorial is inserted. Real, signed and zero cycle coefficients are allowed.

For source calibration choose an auxiliary metric and covolumes a_sigma, with a_vertex=1. A basis of saturated N_tau followed by a primitive quotient lift is a basis of N_sigma; base-times-height gives pr_(tauperp)n=(a_sigma/a_tau)nu, nu inward UNIT. Lattice cycle weights c become Euclidean weights a_sigma c with zero unit-conormal sum. Embed x as (x,1), product metric, to meet BBGS's hyperplane convention without changing tangents. Subtract an ambient extension of f_tau; balance and tangential continuity cancel it. For BBGS's negative unit-normal product B, B_(-f)(ac)(tau)=a_tau D_fc(tau). Iterate this identity in every dimension, including signed/zero intermediates, down to a_vertex=1.

The whole elementary BBGS proof chain is reconstructed. At an actual codimension-two face of one top cell, the two-dimensional quotient has two boundary facets, even for a nonsimplicial cell. For boundary unit directions v1=(1,0), v2=(cos theta,sin theta), the inward perpendiculars (0,1),(sin theta,-cos theta) have paired expansions v1perp=a v1+b v2 and v2perp=a v2+b v1, a=-cot theta, b=csc theta. Expanding the double product groups symmetric diagonal terms and paired cross terms; exchanging the facets interchanges those cross terms and proves commutation. Refinement has exactly three cases: a new facet in an old weighted affine cell cancels equal opposite normals; a subdivided old facet keeps weights/conormal; a face in an old higher-dimensional cell inherits zero. Ambient linear annihilation is equivalent to zero conormal sum, so commutation preserves balancing. This proves the actual 3.12/3.15/3.18/3.19 mechanism, not delegated AR10. For positive intermediate cycles, the local supports from n2 agree tangentially with f_tau; subtracting them in the primitive formula makes all inward residuals nonnegative. This gives genuine finite positive raw products. Relative mixed degree is unchanged because bounded PA functions have zero unbounded-edge slopes and their two bounded-edge degree terms cancel.
